indexes.definition: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX customers_pkey ON benchmark.customers USING btree (customer_id)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX orders_pkey ON benchmark.orders USING btree (order_id)

protocol.baseline: All existing indexes; no experiment indexes
protocol.measurement: Frequency-weighted mean of per-query client execute + fetchall medians
protocol.phase_order: Baseline first in trials 1 and 3; indexed first in trial 2
protocol.summary: Median across trials; improvement is the median of paired percentages
protocol.isolation: One REPEATABLE READ transaction for all measured configurations
protocol.cleanup: Savepoint rollback per configuration and full rollback at the end
protocol.scope: Read performance and added index storage; write costs are not compared here
protocol.selection: Candidate selected on this same workload in a previous experiment; not held-out validation

protocol.cache_policy: warmup rounds; no forced cache clearing
protocol.frequency_usage: aggregation weights; equal repeats per query

queries.sql: SELECT * FROM "benchmark"."orders" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."customer_id" = 2

observations: orders: sequential scan discarded most rows. An index may help; benchmark to confirm.

queries.sql: SELECT * FROM "benchmark"."orders" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."customer_id" = 2 AND "orders"."order_date" >= CAST('2026-01-01' AS DATE)

observations: orders: sequential scan discarded most rows. An index may help; benchmark to confirm.

queries.sql: SELECT * FROM "benchmark"."orders" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."customer_id" = 3 AND "orders"."order_date" >= CAST('2026-06-01' AS DATE)

observations: orders: sequential scan discarded most rows. An index may help; benchmark to confirm.

queries.sql: SELECT * FROM "benchmark"."orders" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."status" = 'delivered'
SELECT * FROM "benchmark"."orders" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."order_date" >= CAST('2026-06-01' AS DATE) AND "orders"."order_date" < CAST('2026-06-08' AS DATE)

observations: orders: sequential scan discarded most rows. An index may help; benchmark to confirm.

queries.sql: SELECT "o"."order_id" AS "order_id", "o"."total_amount" AS "total_amount", "c"."region" AS "region" FROM "benchmark"."orders" AS "o" JOIN "benchmark"."customers" AS "c" ON "o"."customer_id" = "c"."customer_id" WHERE "c"."customer_id" BETWEEN 1 AND 100
SELECT * FROM "benchmark"."orders" AS "orders" WHERE "orders"."customer_id" = 2 ORDER BY "orders"."order_date" DESC LIMIT 20

observations: orders: sequential scan discarded most rows. An index may help; benchmark to confirm.
